previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled with prior DKA admissions, alcohol use disorder, hypertension, and depression presented with altered mental status and dyspnea. She was found to be in severe diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 983 and pH of 6.85, likely due to missed insulin and heavy alcohol use. She was treated in the ICU with IV fluids, an insulin drip, and electrolyte management. She developed transient hypotension requiring pressors and had elevated troponin suggestive of demand ischemia rather than acute coronary syndrome. Her kidney function was impaired on admission with creatinine of 2.0 but improved to 0.7 by discharge. Leukocytosis resolved, and she was transitioned to increased glargine insulin. Antibiotics were briefly given but stopped due to lack of infection. She was discharged home with services, advised to follow up with endocrinology and cardiology for a stress test, and continued on home medications including aspirin, statin, and thiamine.

IMAGING / STUDIES
___ CHEST X-RAY 
Pulmonary vascular congestion.  No focal consolidation. 

___ EKG
Sinus tachycardia. Compared to tracing #1 T waves are not 
peaked.
 
Brief Hospital Course:
___ PMH T1DM, hx DKA, presenting with n/v and DKA in setting of 
medication non-compliance and gastrointestinal illness

ACTIVE ISSUES:
===============
#Diabetic ketoacidosis: Presented in DKA with initial bicarb of 
2. The most likely precipitating factor was non compliance with 
her insulin as her glucometer broke and she was taking 4 U 
Humalog with each meal rather than her prescribed sliding scale. 
She did also report a few days of nausea/vomiting consistent 
with possible viral gastroenteritis.  Urine, CXR, blood cultures 
showed no other evidence of infection. She was started on an 
insulin drip which was uptitrated to 15/hour. Her bicarb 
uptrended on this regimen. She was treated with IVF and 
potassium. On HD2 her glucose was <200 and she was transitioned 
to subcutaneous insulin. Her gap reopened and she briefly had to 
go back on the insulin drip until gap closed again. She also had 
a period of hypoglycemia requiring continuous IV dextrose 
infusion until she was able to reliably take PO.  

___ diabetes followed throughout hospitalization and she was 
discharged on lantus 15 units daily with Humalog sliding scale.  
She met with a diabetes educator and has close ___ followup 
on ___, as well as ___ to aid in her transition home.

#ST depressions and troponinemia: She had a demand NSTEMI during 
a prior DKA episode with no WMA on TTE. This admission she again 
had demand ischemia (ST depressions in lateral leads). EKGs were 
trended and ST depressions improved with resolution of her DKA 
suggestive of demand ischemia. Her troponins were trended and 
peaked at 0.28. She was continued on atorva 80 and her aspirin 
was restarted (she hadn't been taking it at home).  

___: Creatinine 2.4 on admission, from a baseline of ~1. This 
was likely pre-renal due to dehydration and hypotension. 
Lisinopril was held.  Creatinine improved to better than 
baseline, at 0.6, and lisinopril was restarted.

#Hypotension / chronic hypertension: ICU course complicated by 
intermittent hypotension that generally improved with IVF. She 
was briefly on levophed. This was likely hypovolemic. Sepsis was 
considered as alternate etiology but there was no infectious 
source, so antibiotics were not started. 
 
#Leukocytosis / leukopenia
#Chronic anemia: 
Initial leukocytosis likely due to DKA. CXR without evidence of 
pneumonia and UA without signs of infection.  She actually 
trended toward mild leukopenia, suggesting a viral component of 
illness with likely contribution of chronic malnutrition / heavy 
alcohol consumption.  
- Trend as an outpatient

#Alcohol abuse/withdrawal: Patient was a heavy drinker for years 
but denied any prior history of withdrawal, including seizures 
and DTs. She denied recent drinking. She was monitored on CIWA 
but did not require diazepam. She was given thiamine, folate, 
and multivitamins. Social work was consulted and provided 
support and counseling.  Social services formulated plan with 
the patient to re-establish care with Arbour SOAP program for 
substance abuse treatment.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
===============
#Anemia: No clinical evidence of overt bleeding, and H/H 
improving upon discharge.  H/H about stable from prior, with MCV 
100, likely related to alcohol abuse. 

#Depression: Resumed Mirtazapine 30 mg PO QHS and Venlafaxine XR 
225 mg PO DAILY.

#Hypertension: Held Lisinopril 10 in setting of hypotension.  
When her clinical condition stabilized, she became hypertensive 
and amlodipine was added to her regimen
- Ongoing titration of blood pressure medications upon discharge

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
========================
# Poor dentition: Recommend outpatient dental evaluation
# Ongoing titration of blood pressure medications upon discharge
# Close follow-up with ___
# Trend CBC, electrolytes as outpatient 

> 30 minutes on discharge activities, including counseling and
